sources.entry: DSH Desk Pet - Desktop pet that mirrors your coding agent's state, with skins generated from a photo of your own pet.

summary.one_liner: A macOS desktop pet window that changes its mood to match your local DSH coding agent's state, with custom skins that can be generated from a photo of your own pet.
summary.what_it_does: It shows a floating, always-on-top macOS window with a pet that cycles through six states: idle, working, waiting for you, error, happy, and sleeping. The state follows the local DSH (agent) session automatically, with no configuration needed. Clicking the pet expands a list of DSH sessions and what each is doing; right-click gives a menu with do-not-disturb, skins, position, project page, update check, and quit. Users can pick from five bundled skins, or use a bundled skill that asks their own agent/image tool to expand a single picture into 18 poses (six states, three frames each) saved under ~/.dsh-desk-pet/skins/. The README says it runs with the system Python and has no third-party dependencies.
use_cases: Show coding agent status at a glance on the desktop
Turn a photo of a pet into a desktop companion skin
Monitor which DSH sessions are still running
Keep an always-visible status indicator over fullscreen apps
Run a lightweight background desk pet without extra installs
how_to_run: git clone the repository and run ./bin/dsh-desk-pet (standalone, without DSH)
stack: Python (system python, used by the launcher)
notable: Mirrors the state of a local DSH coding agent: idle, working, waiting, error, happy, sleeping
Custom skins generated from a single photo via a bundled skill, stored outside the plugin folder so upgrades don't delete them
Zero dependencies: no compile step and no ffmpeg needed
Sleep mode triggers only when both the agent and the mouse are idle for 90 seconds
Runs as a background process detached from the launching terminal
caveats: macOS only; Windows and Linux are not supported and not planned short-term
Generating a custom skin uses the user's own image tool and quota (18 images), with two confirmation pauses and no progress display during generation
Transparent margin around the pet does not pass clicks through to windows behind it; no docked mini mode in this version
